We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases for JsonSchemaFactory covering all methods. Need to start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Provide a Java file with imports, test class. Must test builder, getInstance, checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml, idMatchesSourceUri, getSchema (string, InputStream, URI), uriFactory, uriTranslator, handling errors, cache behavior.

We can use mocks for URIFactory, URIFetcher, URNFactory, JsonMetaSchema, ValidationContext, JsonSchema etc. But many classes are internal; we can create simple dummy implementations to satisfy behavior. For methods that rely on actual schema parsing we can use a simple schema JSON string like {"type":"object"} and default meta schema via built-in draft.

Simplify: Use JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(SpecVersion.VersionFlag.V4) to get a real factory with built-in meta schema. Then test getSchema(String) returns non-null, and that defaultMetaSchemaURI normalized.

Test normalizeMetaSchemaUri: valid URI transforms scheme to https and removes fragment/query.

Test normalizeMetaSchemaUri throws exception for malformed URI.

Test isYaml: create URI with .yaml, .yml, .json, no extension.

Test idMatchesSourceUri: Use a mock JsonMetaSchema that returns id from schema node. We can create a simple subclass of JsonMetaSchema? Might be abstract. In library, JsonMetaSchema is a class that contains readId method. But we could use reflection to access private method? Actually we can instantiate JsonMetaSchema? It likely has a constructor requiring URI and other parameters. Instead, we can test through public getSchema(URI, JsonNode) where idMatchesSourceUri is exercised. Provide a schema node with "$id": "http://example.com/schema". Provide schemaUri same. Use factory built with custom meta schema? The factory's jsonMetaSchemas map includes default meta schema. That meta schema's readId method probably reads "$id". We'll assume it works.

Cache behavior: call getSchema(URI) twice with same URI pointing to a resource (maybe using classpath resource). Use a temporary file with JSON schema. Since enableUriSchemaCache default true, second call should retrieve from cache. We can verify that fetcher is called only once by using a custom URIFetcher that counts calls. Provide builder with custom fetcher for "file" scheme.

Simplify: Use builder to set custom URIFactory and URIFetcher for "test" scheme, returning InputStream from a string. Then call getSchema(new URI("test://schema.json")) twice, verify fetcher count.

Will need to implement minimal URIFactory that returns the same URI; and URIFetcher that returns ByteArrayInputStream.

Also test builder's default behavior: builder().defaultMetaSchemaURI(...).addMetaSchema(...).build() works.

Edge cases: checkVersion null returns null, unsupported throws IllegalArgumentException.

Test getInstance deprecated returns non-null.

Alright produce test class JsonSchemaFactoryTest with several @Test methods.

Will need imports: org.junit.*, static org.junit.Assert.*, java.net.URI, java.io.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper, com.networknt.schema.*.

Implement custom classes inside test file.

Proceed.
